articles.title: How RAG Works: Embeddings, Vector Search, and Why Your AI App Needs Retrieval
articles.excerpt: A language model knows a lot, but it does not know your data. It has never seen your company's internal documents, your course notes, last week's policy update, or the contents of your database. It al…
articles.body: A language model knows a lot, but it does not know your data. It has never seen your company's internal documents, your course notes, last week's policy update, or the contents of your database. It also has a training cutoff, so it can be out of date, and when it does not know something it sometimes produces a confident, fluent, wrong answer. Fine-tuning a model on your data is possible but slow, expensive, and awkward to keep current. The dominant practical solution is Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): instead of asking the model to remember your information, you look up the relevant pieces at question time and hand them to the model along with the question.

articles.body: This week, something insane is happening. First of all 'Rockstar GTA 6 is launching. And I do not mean “a few gamers will download it” kind of insane. articles.excerpt: Voyager 1 is celebrating a big milestone as it approaches its 50th birthday: reaching one light-day away from Earth.
articles.body: Voyager 1 is celebrating a big milestone as it approaches its 50th birthday: reaching one light-day away from Earth. NASA's long-running interstellar Voyager 1 probe will mark one light-day of distance from Earth on Nov. 18, when the spacecraft is 49 years, two months and 11 days old. The agency recently stated the record distance, which will be reached at 5:16:07 a.m. EST (101607 GMT) is "a huge milestone by any measure, and a day worth celebrating." During the light-day crossover, Voyager will be in contact with the Madrid station of the three-antenna Deep Space Network that monitors all deep-space missions. The spacecraft is currently making its way through the constellation Ophiuchus from the perspective of Earth, said Jeffrey Hayes, a NASA official whose work includes Voyager 1.

articles.title: Vulcan rocket fails, destroying 40 Amazon Leo satellites
articles.excerpt: ULA Vulcan rocket lifts off on November 15, 2026, carrying 40 Amazon Leo broadband satellites. | Photo: Manuel Mazzanti / NurPhoto via Getty Images United Launch Alliance (ULA) suffered what is report…
articles.body: ULA Vulcan rocket lifts off on November 15, 2026, carrying 40 Amazon Leo broadband satellites. | Photo: Manuel Mazzanti / NurPhoto via Getty Images United Launch Alliance (ULA) suffered what is reportedly its first mission failure in its 20-year history, failing to deliver 40 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit. Leo is Amazon's competitor to SpaceX's Starlink, but it has struggled to get off the ground so far, putting only a small portion of the necessary satellites to challenge Starlink into orbit. Today's launch was supposed to be the first of 38 flights Amazon purchased from ULA.

articles.title: 30 years ago, 'Space Jam' proposed the best way to resolve interplanetary disputes
articles.excerpt: Sufferin' succotash! The Monstars and Tune Squad interplanetary slam arrived 30 years ago, and it's still a clinic in interplanetary conflict resolution.
articles.body: You just ordered a Pizza Hut and a two-liter bottle of Mountain Dew. You put on "Space Jam" to watch the greatest of all time team up with the Looney Tunes. It's a perfect evening… in 1996 or 2026. The entire concept of "Space Jam" is so '90s that you swear you can hear Los Del Rio in the background mouthing, "Dale a tu cuerpo alegría, Macarena." As ridiculous as an intergalactic basketball match may sound, it's a perfect example of how even the strangest idea can work if you commit to it fully. In case you thought you hallucinated the whole thing, no, you didn't, as the Looney Tunes find themselves in quite the predicament in this live-action-animation hybrid.
